title: Gemini 2.5 models extended indefinitely for aactive users
content:
This page documents updates to the Gemini API.
September 18, 2026
- Gemini 2.5 models access update: To ensure reliable performance for everyone, we are limiting access to the 2.5 models to users who have actively used them in the past. These models are not deprecated and will continue to be served until further notice through the API. For any new projects, use our latest models: 3.5 Flash-Lite or 3.8 Flash. This helps us maintain sufficient capacity for both ongoing legacy workflows and new applications.
September 17, 2026
- Antigravity Agent 09-2026: Released antigravity-preview-09-2026 ,
which replaces and deprecatesantigravity-preview-05-2026 .If you run on a remote sandbox ( environment: "remote" ) and read onlyoutput_text ormodel_output steps, update the agent string and nothing
else changes.If you run tools locally ( local_environment ) or parsefunction_call steps, the built-in tools changed. Parameters use PascalCase instead of
snake_case, and file edits use line-range replacements instead of full
rewrites.See the Antigravity Agent guide. antigravity-preview-05-2026 shuts down on October 5, 2026, tracked on the
deprecations page.
September 15, 2026
- Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking generally available (GA): Released two new audio-to-audio models for real-time voice applications using the Live API: 
  - Gemini 3.8 Live (gemini-3.8-live ): The default option
for most low-latency voice agent experiences and real-time dialogue
without reasoning delays. Features interleaved reasoning, default
asynchronous function calling, and full session client content updates.
  - Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
(gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking ): High-reasoning
audio-to-audio model supporting background reasoning during live audio
interactions, recommended when higher background reasoning is required.
 To get started, see the Live API guide, the Capabilities guide, and the Thinking guide.

1080p and 4K outputs are generated using upscaling.

report.summary: Google will keep serving Gemini 2.5 models indefinitely to developers who already use them, while routing all new projects to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and 3.8 Flash.
report.background: Since the 2.5 generation launched, Google's Gemini API has moved at an unusually fast release cadence: 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 Flash, live audio models, video generation and transcription models all shipped within roughly a year. That speed creates a cleanup problem. Older endpoints consume serving capacity, yet abruptly deprecating them breaks production systems that teams spent months tuning prompts, evals and cost models around. Google's answer is a middle path: no formal deprecation, no shutdown date, but a gate that only lets previously active users keep calling 2.5. It mirrors a broader industry pattern where labs manage scarce inference capacity by grandfathering legacy traffic while steering new demand to cheaper, more efficient current-generation models.
key_points: No deprecation, no deadline: Gemini 2.5 models are not being retired and will keep serving API traffic 'until further notice,' but only to accounts that have actively used them before. There is no published shutdown date, so existing pipelines are not forced to migrate on a fixed schedule.

New projects are redirected: Google explicitly tells anyone starting fresh to use Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite or Gemini 3.8 Flash. That effectively freezes 2.5 as a legacy-only tier rather than removing it, pushing new capacity demand onto newer, more token-efficient models.

The stated reason is capacity, not capability: Google frames the change as keeping 'sufficient capacity for both ongoing legacy workflows and new applications.' It is a resource-allocation decision that avoids the reputational hit of a hard deprecation announcement.

The surrounding changelog shows how far ahead the current line is: Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.8 Live audio models, Lyria 3.5 music, 3.5 Transcribe and Omni video are all GA. The 2.5 family is now several generations behind on features such as agentic video understanding and Live API improvements.

Legacy means frozen: staying on 2.5 keeps compatibility but forfeits new capabilities, price improvements and bug fixes delivered to the 3.x line. Silent stagnation, not a shutdown, is the practical risk for teams that never migrate.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is another data point that model lifetimes are now managed as capacity contracts rather than versioned software releases: grandfathered access buys goodwill without committing to perpetual serving. For developers, the upside is breathing room — no forced migration sprint — but the downside is an indefinite limbo where you can neither count on 2.5 forever nor benefit from 3.x gains. Teams should treat 2.5 as a frozen dependency, budget migration work, and abstract model calls behind an internal interface. For regular users, the change is mostly invisible, though apps built on 2.5 will gradually fall behind newer products in latency, cost and features like real-time voice and video.
report.tools: Follow the official Gemini API changelog and deprecations page, and Google AI Studio for testing 3.5 Flash-Lite and 3.8 Flash side by side. For migration, review the Latest Gemini model guide and Vertex AI model versions. A model-abstraction layer such as LiteLLM, OpenRouter, LangChain or LlamaIndex makes swapping endpoints cheaper, while prompt-eval harnesses like Promptfoo or Weights & Biases Weave help verify parity before you cut over.
